location: Washington, D.C.; Reading, PA; West Chester, PA
description: The Office of Representative Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA-06) is accepting applications for Fall 2025 Press Interns in our Washington, D.C., Reading, and West Chester offices. This internship will run from mid-late August through early December. We offer stipends to applicants. Our internship program has returned to in-person work with flexible telework options. Ideal applicants are adaptable and proactive self-starters who have experience in a fast-paced, deadline-oriented work environment. Press interns will be responsible for compiling and distributing press clips, helping draft copy for press and digital materials, and developing digital content. Press interns will have the opportunity to staff the congresswoman to capture videos and photos of events. We offer interns the opportunity to see Congress up close and from the inside.
responsibilities: Compiling and distributing press clips
Helping draft copy for press and digital materials
Developing digital content
Staffing the congresswoman to capture videos and photos of events
qualifications: Adaptable and proactive self-starter
Experience in a fast-paced, deadline-oriented work environment
Independent problem-solver
Strong writing skills
Comfortable communicating to both internal and external audiences
Technical experience with graphic design tools (Canva, InDesign, Illustrator), photo editing programs (Photoshop, Lightroom), or video editing software (Premiere, Headliner) a major plus
Prior volunteer, leadership, and work experience are a plus
Ties to PA-06 are also a plus
how_to_apply: Send 1) a resume, 2) ONE brief paragraph about yourself and why you're interested in interning in our office, 3) a writing sample, and 4) one example of digital work (video, graphic or photo) to PA06Press.Interships@mail.house.gov.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.

location: West Chester, PA; Reading, PA; Washington, D.C.
description: The Office of Representative Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA-06) is accepting applications for Fall 2025 legislative interns in our West Chester, Reading, and Washington, D.C. offices. This internship will run from late mid-late August through early December. Both full and part time internships are available, and we offer stipends to applicants. Our internship program has returned to in-person work with flexible telework options should interns need to work from home. Ideal applicants are self-starters who bring a customer service mindset and a passion for community service. Applicants must be intellectually curious, willing to spend a lot of time on the phone and write well. Responsibilities range from helping constituents, to doing research and drafting memos for our legislative staff, to staffing the Congresswoman in hearings or meetings. We offer interns the opportunity to see Congress up close and from the inside. Prior volunteer, leadership, and work experience are a plus. Ties to PA-06 are also a plus. Please submit applications through the "Legislative Internship" form our website, Houlahan.house.gov by July 13, 2025. Due to a high volume of applicants, you will likely only be contacted if you are selected for an interview. This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status. Women, people of color, and other members of traditionally underrepresented communities are strongly encouraged to apply.
responsibilities: Helping constituents
Doing research and drafting memos for legislative staff
Staffing the Congresswoman in hearings or meetings
qualifications: Self-starter with a customer service mindset
Passion for community service
Intellectually curious
Willing to spend a lot of time on the phone
Ability to write well
Prior volunteer, leadership, and work experience are a plus
Ties to PA-06 are also a plus
how_to_apply: Submit applications through the "Legislative Internship" form on Houlahan.house.gov by July 13, 2025.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.

description: Congressman Mike Levin (CA-49) seeks press and legislative interns for his Washington, D.C., office for the Fall 2025 term. These internships provide an opportunity for undergraduate students, graduate students, and recent graduates to learn more about the workings of a Congressional office and the legislative process. Internships last approximately three to four months and are intended to be an educational experience. Internships are offered for either academic credit or a stipend. Current students and recent graduates will be given first priority for the internship program. Applicants with strong ties to the 49th District are given preference.
responsibilities: Attending committee hearings and congressional briefings
Conducting policy research and drafting legislative materials
Authoring constituent correspondence on a range of policy issues
Answering phones and processing mail
Leading constituents on tours of the Capitol
Working on other administrative and legislative tasks, as directed
Assisting the Communications Director and Digital Manager/Press Secretary in drafting and editing social media content, digital graphics, and other digital materials
Drafting press releases, newsletters, remarks, and talking points
Compiling daily press clips and maintaining press lists
Working on other administrative and communications-related tasks, as directed
qualifications: Must be a high school graduate
General understanding of the U.S. political system
Value open communication and be eager to grow
Bring a can-do attitude
Press interns should have strong social media skills and basic familiarity with graphic design and video editing
Submission of a sample graphic or similar communications work with application is strongly encouraged
how_to_apply: Email a cover letter, resume, three references, and a brief writing sample all in one pdf file, with the file name including internship class, year, last name, and first name (i.e. Fall2025.Doe.Jane.pdf) to CA49.DCInternships@mail.house.gov by July 15. Specify whether you are applying for the press internship or the legislative internship.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer; we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity or expression, or sexual orientation.

description: The House Committee on Energy and Commerce, Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations (Democratic Staff) is seeking a Law Clerk for Fall 2025 to assist in conducting oversight and investigations of issues within the Committee's broad jurisdiction. Law Clerks will work closely with Subcommittee counsel and professional staff on a wide range of issues related to the environment, energy, health care, and consumer protection sectors. This is a paid position. Law clerks will receive a stipend, and applicants may request the Committee's assistance to receive credit from their educational institution.
responsibilities: Assisting in the preparation for Congressional hearings
Contributing to the management of investigations of governmental and private entities
Conducting research, document review, and analysis
Drafting letters, memoranda, and investigative reports
Coordinating with other Subcommittees of the full Committee
qualifications: In at least their second year of law school or a recent law school graduate
Detail-oriented and proactive problem-solver
Strong communication skills
Strong legal research and writing skills
how_to_apply: Submit a resume, cover letter, and short writing sample to InternshipResume.EC@mail.house.gov with the subject line "E&C O&I Law Clerk." Applications are due on June 30, 2025.
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, national origin, disability, military status, age, marital status, or parental status.

location: Washington, D.C. and Little Rock, AR
description: Congressman French Hill (AR02) has internship positions available for the Fall 2025 term in both his DC and Little Rock offices. Interns will work in a fast-paced environment, gaining valuable exposure and knowledge of the legislative process and the U.S. Congress while helping central Arkansans. The office offers paid and unpaid internships depending on availability. Applications should be submitted by June 30 but will be accepted on a rolling basis until all positions are filled.
responsibilities: Answering constituent phone calls
Assisting staff with administrative tasks
Conducting legislative research
Assisting with correspondence
qualifications: Positive attitude
Strong work ethic
Excellent written and oral communication skills
Detail-oriented self-starter
Ability to take and listen to direction
Willingness to work both independently and as part of a team
Working knowledge of current events and policy topics
Willingness to assist with daily office tasks
Arkansas ties strongly preferred
Open to college and graduate students as well as recent graduates
how_to_apply: Send a resume and cover letter to AR02.Applications@mail.house.gov indicating which location you are applying for. Applications should be submitted by June 30 but will be accepted on a rolling basis until all positions are filled. For questions, contact the office at (202) 225-2506.

description: Congresswoman Suzan DelBene, representing the 1st Congressional District of Washington state, seeks interns for her Washington, D.C. and District offices. Interns will work in a fast-paced congressional office, gaining valuable experience and knowledge of the United States Congress. Congressional internships are open to all majors and designed for undergraduate and graduate students, as well as recent graduates with an interest in public service. Starting and ending dates are flexible, although prospective interns should be able to commit to at least 17 hours per week during the internship. A stipend of $1,000/month will be provided to full-time interns, and a stipend of $500/month will be provided to part-time interns. The deadline for Fall 2025 Internship Applications is 11:59 PM on Sunday, July 6, 2025. Due to a high volume of applications, you may only be contacted if you are selected for an interview. No phone calls or walk ins - please email internship.delbene@mail.house.gov with any questions or concerns.
responsibilities: Greeting constituents and handling constituent phone calls
Assisting staff with administrative tasks
Conducting research
Assisting with constituent correspondence
Kirkland, WA interns: attending community events and tours with the Congresswoman and staff
Washington, D.C. interns: leading tours of the U.S. Capitol
Washington, D.C. interns: attending hearings and briefings for the legislative staff
qualifications: Exceptional written and oral communication skills
A high degree of professionalism
A strong interest in public service
Washington state ties are a plus but are not required
Open to all majors; designed for undergraduate and graduate students, as well as recent graduates
Ability to commit to at least 17 hours per week during the internship
how_to_apply: Submit a cover letter, resume, and short writing sample (1 to 2 pages) through the online form. The deadline for Fall 2025 Internship Applications is 11:59 PM on Sunday, July 6, 2025.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.

description: The office of U.S. Congressman Jeff Van Drew (Republican-NJ-02) is currently accepting applications for his Washington, D.C. office for full and part-time interns for the fall internship session. This is a conservative office, so each intern will be required to express the Congressman's conservative perspective to constituents and people who call into the office. The start date would be as early as August 6th (flexible depending on availability) with a flexible end date. Interns are paid a stipend based on availability and have access to transit benefits. The internship will offer students and young professionals invaluable experience with our nation's legislative process. Interns contribute to the daily operations of the office and are expected to act in a reliable, professional manner at all times. Congressman Van Drew supports students requesting credit for their internship through their university.
responsibilities: Greeting visitors
Answering phones
Leading tours of the Capitol
Opening and sorting mail
Attending briefings
Performing legislative research
Various other tasks to assist staff
qualifications: Must express the Congressman's conservative perspective to constituents and callers
Must act in a reliable, professional manner at all times
Available for full or part-time work during the fall internship session
how_to_apply: Email a resume and cover letter to nj02internships@mail.house.gov. Indicate in your cover letter that you are applying for a fall internship and format the files as [Full Name_Resume], [Full Name_Cover Letter].
